name: Cysts and Fistulae of the Face and Oral Cavity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Facial and Oral Cysts and Fistulae

criteria.description: Presence of visible or palpable cystic swelling or fistulous tract on the face or within the oral cavity
Radiological evidence (CT, MRI, or ultrasound) demonstrating cystic lesion or fistulous tract in facial/oral soft tissues or bone
Histopathological confirmation of cyst lining or fistula tract with characteristic epithelial or inflammatory features
Exclusion of infectious causes such as abscess or cellulitis by microbiological studies
History of recurrent swelling, discharge, or drainage from facial/oral site

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus imaging confirmation and histopathological evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, radiological, and pathological correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable cystic swelling of the face or oral mucosa
searchTerms: noticeable cystic swelling on face or mouth
palpable fluid-filled lump in oral area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent fistulous tract with mucopurulent discharge

searchTerms: localized swelling or lump on face

common.symptomName: Recurrent localized inflammation or erythema over lesion
searchTerms: repeated redness and swelling over lesion

common.symptomName: Oral mucosal ulceration adjacent to cyst or fistula
searchTerms: mouth ulcer near cyst or fistula

common.symptomName: Intermittent serous or purulent drainage from fistula
searchTerms: intermittent clear or pus drainage from fistula

occasional.symptomName: Mild localized pain or tenderness at lesion site
searchTerms: mild pain or tenderness at lesion

occasional.symptomName: Foul odor from oral cavity related to fistula
searchTerms: bad smell from mouth related to fistula
unpleasant mouth smell due to infection

rare.symptomName: Facial nerve palsy due to lesion extension
searchTerms: drooping face due to nerve damage

rare.symptomName: Systemic signs of infection such as fever

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)
Negative bacterial cultures in non-infectious cysts
imaging: CT or MRI showing well-defined cystic lesions or fistulous tracts
Ultrasound demonstrating anechoic or hypoechoic cystic structures
other: Histopathology showing cyst lined by epithelium or fistula tract with granulation tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Acute onset with systemic signs of infection
Typical location along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid

redFlags: Neurological deficits such as facial nerve palsy
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
references: Orphanet: Cysts and fistulae of the face and oral cavity - ORPHA:155835
